Perplex

per-PLEKS · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To perplex to completely confuse or baffle someone, usually with something puzzling.

The disappearing-coin trick perplexed the entire birthday party, including the parents.

Worked Example

The detective was perplexed by a locked-room murder scene that seemed to have no possible entry point for the killer.

Perplex fits a genuinely puzzling problem or mystery -- something with no obvious answer -- more than everyday confusion.

How Strong Is It? — puzzle → perplex → stupefy

puzzle vs. perplex

puzzle vs. perplex: Puzzle is weaker than perplex: a single odd word choice might puzzle a reader briefly, but an argument that perplexes leaves them thoroughly and completely baffled.

stupefy vs. perplex

stupefy vs. perplex: To be stupefied is to be left in a stunned, almost dazed state of confusion.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — per-

prefix — per-: thoroughly, throughout (Latin per-)

root — -plex

root — -plex: woven, entangled (Latin plectere/plexus)

Put it together

Put it together: Perplex comes from Latin per- ("thoroughly") + plexus ("woven, entangled") -- literally something thoroughly tangled, which came to describe a mind tangled up in confusion.

Use the root in a new word: complex

Use the root in a new word: complex: A complex machine has so many interconnected moving parts that a single manual isn't enough to explain it.
